The prediction successfully identified the key policy levers (tariffs, asset purchases) that would drive market outcomes, though the full inflationary impact may have been masked by temporary data anomalies and firm-level tariff absorption in 2025.

While tariff upside risks were real, firms absorbed much of the impact, preventing the inflation spike NatWest anticipated.

overall_analysis: NatWest's prediction was directionally correct about inflation risks but materially overestimated the magnitude of the inflation spike from tariffs. They correctly identified that Trump policies posed upside risks to core goods prices, but underestimated firms' ability to absorb tariff costs and the continued disinflationary forces in the economy. Their 3.2% PCE forecast proved too high by approximately 50-60 basis points.
